subject: Pilot commitment phasing / buyer approval path for AWS Private Offer
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@maplefin.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@maplefin.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot commitment phasing / buyer approval path for AWS Private Offer

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the demo last week — the infra folks liked the latency numbers. Procurement asked me to clarify a couple things before we open a private offer request in AWS Marketplace:

1) We want a 3-month pilot with an option to convert to an annual commitment. Can the Private Offer reflect an initial 3-month term that auto-converts, or do we need two separate offers?
2) Who at our side needs to sign for the pilot vs. the annual? Our finance team says pilots under $25k can be approved by the BU director but anything >$25k needs CFO approval.
3) Pricing: can you give a line-item for pilot pricing (discounted hourly) and the committed-rate if we convert within the 90-day window?

Also — we have a vendor onboarding checklist for security evidence. Is there a one-page checklist you can attach? Procurement will route faster if we can attach the PO template they expect.

If easier, we can hop on a 30-min call tomorrow early afternoon.

Thanks,
Jordan
Senior Cloud Architect
Maple Financial

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@maplefin.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot commitment phasing / buyer approval path for AWS Private Offer

Jordan — really appreciate the clear asks. Quick answers inline, plus next steps below.

1) Term modeling: AWS Private Offer can be created as either a short-term (3mo) offer or as an annual with a conditional conversion. Practically, we recommend issuing a 3-month Private Offer (pilot) with a simple conversion clause in the SOW/Order that triggers a change to the annual SKU and pricing. That keeps activation simple on AWS side and avoids two separate marketplace activations.

2) Approvals: Good to know your internal threshold. On our side: vendor acceptance of a PO for a pilot typically requires BU director + procurement acknowledgement. Conversion to an annual commitment will require signature from your CFO (per your policy) — we can include a one-click conversion acceptance link in the renewal notice to streamline routing.

3) Pricing: Vivek is looping in suggested pilot hourly and the committed annual effective rate. We can hold the pilot rate for 90 days and credit pilot consumption against the first month of annual committed spend if they convert.

Attachments: I attached a lightweight PO template that procurement prefers (Maple_PO_template_v1.docx) and a draft pilot schedule (MOU_pilot-schedule.xlsx). Also linking our security onboarding checklist in the notes.

Next steps (proposed):
- Vivek to confirm pilot vs committed pricing bands (by EOD)
- Jordan / procurement to confirm PO approval owner and any legal must-haves for the pilot conversion clause
- If accepted, we’ll draft the Private Offer and pilot SOW for your review (goal: send by Wed EOD)

If you want a quick call, Vanessa has availability Wed 10:00–11:00 PT.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Sr. Marketplace Partnerships | Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@maplefin.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 14:29:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot commitment phasing / buyer approval path for AWS Private Offer

Jordan / Priya — pricing proposal below. Kept it tight to make procurement routing simpler.

Pilot (3 months):
- SKU: RW-PILOT-M1
- Pilot discounted hourly: $0.42/hr (list equivalent $0.65/hr)
- Estimated pilot spend cap: $18,000 (we recommend capping to avoid surprise approvals)

Conversion to annual (if conversion notice given within 90 days of pilot start):
- Annual committed SKU: RW-ANNUAL-S1
- Committed effective blended rate: $0.30/hr
- Pilot credit: Pilot consumption dollars up to $18k applied as credit to first invoice in annual term

Notes on AWS Private Offer flow:
- We will create a one-off Private Offer for the pilot with the SKU and a 90-day conversion clause in the SOW. AWS marketplace requires the private offer activation and then buyer acceptance; conversion will be a separate marketplace amendment that references the pilot PO (we’ll draft the language).
- Approval gating: to avoid CFO signoff on a pilot, we can keep the pilot cap <= $25k as you requested. If you anticipate >$25k consumption, we can split the pilot (cap + overage approval) or require CFO signoff upfront.

I’ll prepare the price lines for the Private Offer creation; Priya / Vanessa please confirm acceptance and I’ll upload to the marketplace tile.

Vivek
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@maplefin.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot commitment phasing / buyer approval path for AWS Private Offer

Jordan — thanks for the quick turn. Per Vivek’s numbers, we’ll proceed with the pilot PO template attached. A few operational clarifications:

- PO fields: please fill "Estimated Pilot Cap" and sign by the BU director. Procurement should attach that signed PO when accepting the Private Offer activation in AWS.
- Legal redline: We added one small sentence to the SOW to handle conversion timing ("Buyer must provide written conversion notice no later than 7 days before pilot expiry to qualify for the pilot credit"). If your legal needs different wording, send proposed language and we’ll accept or counter quickly.
- Activation timeline: once we have signed PO and procurement confirmation we’ll create the Private Offer and send the AWS activation link (target: 24–48 hours).

I’ve attached the PO template and pilot schedule. Jordan — can you confirm by EOD Thursday who will sign the PO (name + title) so we can include that in the Private Offer metadata?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Marketplace Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
